name: Torus
description: Self-renewing circulation geometry enabling perpetual energy exchange and feedback stability.

core_attributes.pattern: cyclic flow, self-referential feedback, symmetry preservation

scope.definition: Proportion of plasma confinement events in toroidal magnetic geometry (tokamak/stellarator) achieving ≥1 second stability, compared to 0% in equivalent linear or cylindrical geometries at the same field strength. Measures the topological advantage of toroidal closure.

evidence.source: Wesson (2011) 'Tokamaks', 4th ed., Oxford; JET experimental data 1983-2020 (European Fusion Development Agreement); historical comparison with linear pinch experiments (1950s-1960s) which achieved <0.01s confinement.
cross_domain_examples: smoke ring (Kelvin vortex ring) persistence in still air — toroidal vorticity self-stabilizes
Saturn ring system: toroidal orbit stability over 4 billion years
cardiac left ventricular vortex ring: blood flow optimization during diastole
toroidal solenoid for electromagnetic shielding (near-zero external field)

scope.falsifiability: If a non-toroidal magnetic geometry achieves equivalent plasma confinement time at equivalent field strength, the topological advantage of torus closure is not the determining factor.
scope.measurement_limits: Confinement time varies with plasma temperature, field strength, and instability modes. Value represents ITER-class parameters; earlier tokamaks show 0.6-0.8. The topological advantage is real but not sufficient alone — field configuration and plasma shaping matter.
